key: Excellent Savitar hath mounted up on high for you, ye sure and careful Guides. Bipeds and quadrupeds, with several hopes and aims, and birds have settled to their tasks.
s: A hymn to all the gods, seeking their gifts at dawn, noon and dusk, here greets the rising sun; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.27.12, reads the creatures’ tasks as some men performing the Agnihotra, others praising the gods, and beasts roaming to graze.

evidence.gloss: Seeking (arthinaḥ), the two-footed, men with two feet, the four-footed, horses and the like with four feet, and the flying, the birds, settle (ny aviśran) each into his own work. When the sun has risen some men perform the Agnihotra and the like, some make praise addressed to the gods; cattle and the like roam everywhere to eat grass and the like.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 8.27.12 at [646,12]); the packet’s Sanskrit (ud u ṣya vaḥ savitā ... ni dvipādaś catuṣpādo arthino ’viśran patayiṣṇavaḥ) is the app’s verse. Sāyaṇa takes ny aviśran as each settling to his own work and spells it out: at sunrise some men perform (kurvanti) the Agnihotra and like rites, some praise the gods, beasts roam to graze. One change: the proposal said the men are ‘beginning’ the Agnihotra; his word is kurvanti, perform, so the sentence now reads ‘performing’. Plain sense faithful: Wilson’s introduction gives the Viśvedevas as deities, and 8.27.19 to 21 ask the gods’ gifts at sunrise, noon and evening; no four-word run from the key.
